passage.title: VOL 6 Test 4 - Petro power: an eco-revolution?
paragraphs: Laura Ingalls Wilders semi-autobiographical novel The Long Winter describes how the inhabitants of a small town called De smet in the american mid-west narrowly avoided starvation during the severe winter of 1880-1881.Over three metres of snow fell on the northern plains, immobilising the railways and cutting off the settlers from the rest of the world. Laura and her neighbours were only saved when her fiancé trudged 30 kilometres through the snow to fetch food, risking their lives in the process. The story is a reminder of how lethal geographical isolation and crop failures could be before the advent of modern farming and transportation technologies. Not long ago, subsistence farmers in many countries had to cope with the ’lean season’ - the period of greatest scarcity before new crops became available. In England, late spring was once referred to as ’the hungry gap’. The situation was made worse by the cost of moving heavy things over muddy roads. Three centuries ago, moving goods 50 kilometres on land between, say, Liverpool and Manchester was as expensive as shipping them across the north Atlantic.

The development of coal-powered railways and steamships in the 19th century revolutionized the lives of farmers. Instead of having to grow everything they needed, they could now specialise in what they did in best and rely on other producers for their remaining needs. The result was not only food and ever-cheaper prices, but the end of widespread famine and starvation, as the surplus from regions with good harvests could now be transported to those that had experienced mediocre ones. Since then, petroleum-derived fuels have largely displaced coal because of their higher energy density, cleaner combustion and greater ease of extraction, further improving road and rail transportation systems.

While the convenience of modern methods of transportation is obvious, few people grasp their historical significance in terms of their beneficial impact on large cities and the health of residents. In 1898, delegates gathered in New York City for the world’s first international urban-planning conference.

The topic that dominated discussions was not infrastructure or housing, but horse manure. The problem was that as the populations of cities like New York and London grew, the number of horses there also grew, and in New York the production nearly one million kilograms of manure each day. If this problem continued it was estimated that by 1950 every street in London would be buried three metres deep in horse manure. Unable to think of any solution, the delegates concluded that urban living was becoming unsustainable.

Paradoxically, much of the urban manure problem was related to the growth of the railways. The ability to deliver perishable goods, such as meat and dairy products, from locations that benefited from better soil and climate, put many farms based near cities out of business. As these had relied on manure from city workhorses for fertiliser, the demand for this was greatly reduced. The impact of urban workhorses was felt both in the cities and in the countryside. In cities, apart from their overwhelming stench, the manure piles were prime breeding grounds for house flies, perhaps three billion of which hatched each day in US cities in the early 20th century. With flies came outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria. Workhorses sometimes panicked in heavy traffic and kicked or bit bystanders. The clatter of wagon wheels on cobblestone pavement could be deafening, and since a single wagon occupied more street space than a modern truck, they also created significant traffic congestion, while a horse that collapsed on the road created an obstruction that was difficult to remove. The countryside also suffered. To supply the workhorses with oats and hay, additional land had to be cleared of its natural animal life and vegetation, and sometimes water had to be diverted to irrigate it, with considerable negative effects on the whole area.

So, while the trains, cars and trucks of the early 20th century were noisy and polluting by today’s standards, they were regarded as a significant improvement on what had gone before. Before they were available, poor soils often meant that a large amount of land was required to sustain a household, and much environmental damage, primarily in the form of soil erosion, was caused by trying to farm these soils. It could be argued that modern transportation allowed the development of remote regions like the Canadian prairies and allowed more suitable crops to be grown in poorer soils in Europe, before being sold elsewhere.

Over time, the concentration of food production in the world’s best locations allowed some agricultural land to revert to a wild state. For instance, France benefited from an expansion of its forest area by one third between 1830 and 1960. This so-called ’forest transition’ occurred in the context of a doubling of the French population and a dramatic increase in standards of living.

Improvements in logistics also allowed and export of food from locations where water was abundant to regions where it was scarce, thus preventing the depletion of water resources there. It also made possible a drastic increase in the size of cities. Contrary to what some people believe, the growth in cities is a positive development. In the words of economist Ed Glaeser, ’Residing in a forest might seem to be a good way of showing one’s love of nature, but living in a concrete jungle is actually far more ecologically friendly... If you love nature, stay away from it! It could be argued that modern transportation technologies have been a major contributor to a wealthier, cleaner and more sustainable world.’

question_groups.instructions:
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter, in boxes 1-4 on your answer sheet.

questions.text: Why were the inhabitants of De Smet in danger of starvation?

options.label: A
options.text: The trains were unable to operate normally.

options.label: B
options.text: The harvest had been completely destroyed.

options.label: C
options.text: The roads to the town had not yet been built.

options.label: D
options.text: The farmers were reluctant to sell their produce.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Tại sao cư dân của De Smet có nguy cơ bị đói? (danger of starvation)
Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Tiểu thuyết bán tự truyện The Long Winter của Laura Ingalls Wilder mô tả cách cư dân của một thị trấn nhỏ tên là De Smet ở miền trung tây nước Mỹ đã suýt chết đói trong mùa đông khắc nghiệt năm 1880-1881. Hơn ba mét tuyết đã rơi xuống các đồng bằng phía bắc, làm tê liệt các tuyến đường sắt và chia cắt những người định cư khỏi phần còn lại của thế giới."
=> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu A (Các chuyến tàu không thể hoạt động bình thường).
Bước 3: Đáp án: A
Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án B -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến việc "mùa màng đã bị phá hủy hoàn toàn".
Đáp án C -> Đoạn văn không đề cập đến việc "các con đường đến thị trấn vẫn chưa được xây dựng".
Đáp án D -> Đoạn văn không nói về việc "nông dân không muốn bán nông sản của họ".
quotes: Laura Ingalls Wilders semi-autobiographical novel The Long Winter describes how the inhabitants of a small town called De smet in the american mid-west narrowly avoided starvation during the severe winter of 1880-1881.Over three metres of snow fell on the northern plains, immobilising the railways and cutting off the settlers from the rest of the world.

questions.text: What problem did subsistence farmers have in the past?

options.label: A
options.text: They had no effective means of storing food.

options.label: B
options.text: Food was expensive because of high shipping costs.

options.label: C
options.text: Their access to food was limited at certain times.

options.label: D
options.text: Food could not be transported for long distances by road.

quotes: Not long ago, subsistence farmers in many countries had to cope with the ’lean season’ - the period of greatest scarcity before new crops became available. In England, late spring was once referred to as ’the hungry gap’.

questions.text: The writer says that the use of coal to power railways and steamships

options.label: A
options.text: led to a greater range of fresh vegetables being available in urban areas.

options.label: B
options.text: was less efficient than the use of petroleum-derived products.

options.label: C
options.text: allowed farmers to be more self-sufficient than they were previously.

options.label: D
options.text: was better for the environment than using petroleum-derived products.

quotes: Since then, petroleum-derived fuels have largely displaced coal because of their higher energy density, cleaner combustion and greater ease of extraction, further improving road and rail transportation systems.

questions.text: The writer refers to an urban planning conference held in 1898 in order to

options.label: A
options.text: illustrate a problem that was later solved by modern technology.

options.label: B
options.text: give an example of poor decisions made about urban planning.

options.label: C
options.text: show that urban issues were misunderstood in the past.

options.label: D
options.text: indicate the disregard at the time for public health concerns.

quotes: In 1898, delegates gathered in New York City for the world’s first international urban-planning conference.

question_groups.body:
Problems caused by urban workhorses
In cities, the large amounts of horse manure led to ____ (5) in the streets and was also linked to the spread of ____ (6). In certain situations, the horses might even cause ____ (7) to passers-by. There were also the problems of noise and congestion caused by horse-drawn vehicles. In the countryside, there were problems too. The ____ (8) was damaged because of the need to provide ____ (9) for urban workhorses.
question_groups.body_html:
Problems caused by urban workhorses

In cities, the large amounts of horse manure led to [5] in the streets and was also linked to the spread of [6]. In certain situations, the horses might even cause [7] to passers-by. There were also the problems of noise and congestion caused by horse-drawn vehicles. In the countryside, there were problems too. The [8] was damaged because of the need to provide [9] for urban workhorses.

quotes: In cities, apart from their overwhelming stench, the manure piles were prime breeding grounds for house flies, perhaps three billion of which hatched each day in US cities in the early 20th century.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
...và cũng liên quan đến sự lây lan của .....
Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN (Danh từ, vì chỗ trống đứng sau cụm "the spread of", chỉ đối tượng bị lây lan)
Dấu hiệu: the spread of + NOUN (NOUN làm Object của Preposition ‘of’)
Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
With flies came outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria. ~ linked to the spread of ....
outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria ~ .... (các loại bệnh)
Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Cùng với ruồi là sự bùng phát của bệnh thương hàn, tả và bạch hầu." (With flies came outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria.) Đây là các loại bệnh tật.
Bước 5: Đáp án: J
...và cũng liên quan đến sự lây lan của bệnh tật. (...and was also linked to the spread of diseases.)
quotes: With flies came outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria.
Workhorses sometimes panicked in heavy traffic and kicked or bit bystanders.

To supply the workhorses with oats and hay, additional land had to be cleared of its natural animal life and vegetation, and sometimes water had to be diverted to irrigate it, with considerable negative effects on the whole area.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
...vì nhu cầu cung cấp .... cho ngựa kéo xe ở thành thị.
Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN (Danh từ, vì chỗ trống đứng sau động từ "provide", chỉ đối tượng được cung cấp)
Dấu hiệu: provide + NOUN (NOUN làm Object của Transitive verb ‘provide’)
Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
To supply the workhorses with oats and hay ~ the need to provide .... for urban workhorses
oats and hay (là thức ăn cho ngựa) ~ ....
Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Để cung cấp yến mạch và cỏ khô cho ngựa kéo xe..." (To supply the workhorses with oats and hay...) Yến mạch và cỏ khô là thức ăn cho ngựa.
Bước 5: Đáp án: C
...vì nhu cầu cung cấp thức ăn cho ngựa kéo xe ở thành thị. (...because of the need to provide food for urban workhorses.)
quotes: To supply the workhorses with oats and hay, additional land had to be cleared of its natural animal life and vegetation, and sometimes water had to be diverted to irrigate it, with considerable negative effects on the whole area.

questions.text: Farmers whose land was poor failed to benefit from modern forms of transport.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những người nông dân có đất đai cằn cỗi đã không được hưởng lợi từ các hình thức vận tải hiện đại.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
poor soils ~ land was poor
allowed more suitable crops to be grown in poorer soils in Europe, before being sold elsewhere ~ benefit from modern forms of transport
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ rằng "có thể cho rằng giao thông vận tải hiện đại... cho phép trồng các loại cây trồng phù hợp hơn trên những vùng đất nghèo nàn hơn ở châu Âu, trước khi được bán đi nơi khác" ("It could be argued that modern transportation allowed... allowed more suitable crops to be grown in poorer soils in Europe, before being sold elsewhere"). Việc trồng được cây phù hợp hơn và bán đi nơi khác chính là một lợi ích.
=> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Nông dân có đất đai cằn cỗi đã không được hưởng lợi" (Farmers whose land was poor failed to benefit).
Bước 4: Đáp án: NO
quotes: It could be argued that modern transportation allowed the development of remote regions like the Canadian prairies and allowed more suitable crops to be grown in poorer soils in Europe, before being sold elsewhere.

questions.text: Between 1830 and 1960 there were positive effects associated with changing patterns of agriculture in France.
quotes: Over time, the concentration of food production in the world’s best locations allowed some agricultural land to revert to a wild state. For instance, France benefited from an expansion of its forest area by one third between 1830 and 1960. This so-called ’forest transition’ occurred in the context of a doubling of the French population and a dramatic increase in standards of living.

questions.text: A fairer distribution of the world's water resources is needed.
quotes: Improvements in logistics also allowed and export of food from locations where water was abundant to regions where it was scarce, thus preventing the depletion of water resources there.

questions.text: Living in the countryside does less harm to the environment than living in a city.
quotes: In the words of economist Ed Glaeser, ’Residing in a forest might seem to be a good way of showing one’s love of nature, but living in a concrete jungle is actually far more ecologically friendly... If you love nature, stay away from it!

questions.text: It is possible that modern developments in transportation have had an effect which is positive.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Có thể là những phát triển hiện đại trong giao thông vận tải đã có một tác động mà...
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
modern developments in transportation ~ modern transportation technologies
have had an effect ~ have been a major contributor
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Có thể lập luận rằng các công nghệ giao thông vận tải hiện đại đã là một đóng góp chính cho một thế giới giàu có hơn, sạch hơn và bền vững hơn".
=> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "có thể là những phát triển hiện đại trong giao thông vận tải đã có một tác động" (It is possible that modern developments in transportation have had an effect).
Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: It could be argued that modern transportation technologies have been a major contributor to a wealthier, cleaner and more sustainable world.’
